2608.02046.title: CompanionBench: A Theory-Anchored, Real-World-Grounded Benchmark for AI Emotional Companionship
2608.02046.paper_summary: LLM companions are deployed at scale in personally consequential settings, yet poorly evaluated. Existing benchmarks use hand-authored scenarios and prompted simulators, aggregate empathy into one score, and overlook judge biases such as same-family favoritism and scale drift. We introduce CompanionBench, an interactive bilingual benchmark. To our knowledge, it is the first companion benchmark to ground both its scenarios and a trained user simulator in de-identified real-world data. A hidden disclosure gate branches each persona's trajectory on the agent's own behavior, controlling the interaction state space without scripting dialogue. We operationalize ten capabilities derived from 25 theories across psychology and counseling, four of them not graded explicitly by prior work: holding ambiguity, selfobject responsiveness, positive resonance and calibrated challenge. Agents are assessed on two complementary axes: a subjective ten-capability rubric and a deterministic measure of whether deeper disclosure was earned. A cross-family panel dilutes same-family favoritism; an Item Response Theory model separates agent quality from judge severity. Theory fixes what to measure and how personas are structured; real data supply events, history, and profiles -- coverage from theory, authenticity from data. Rankings are reproducible in both languages (rho = 0.996 ZH / 0.953 EN). Evaluating 28 agents reveals capability-level differences obscured by aggregate scores. Emotion regulation and calibrated challenge remain common weaknesses; holding ambiguity discriminates most. Role-play agents rank near the bottom: immersion does not imply relational competence. Across agents, the dominant failure mode is substituting surface warmth for substantive relational support. We will release 500 Chinese-English parallel pairs and the evaluation code.
2608.02046.paper_summary_zh: LLM 伴侶在個人影響重大的環境中大規模部署，但評估不佳。現有的基準使用手動編寫的場景和提示模擬器，將同理心聚合為一個分數，並忽視了評審偏見，例如同家庭偏愛和規模漂移。我們介紹 CompanionBench，一個互動的雙語基準。據我們所知，它是第一個將場景和訓練用戶模擬器基於去識別的真實數據的伴侶基準。一個隱藏的披露閘將每個角色的軌跡分支到代理自身的行為上，控制互動狀態空間而不編寫對話。我們將來自心理學和輔導的 25 個理論衍生的十個能力具體化，其中四個在先前的工作中未明確評分：保持模糊性、自我物件反應、正向共鳴和校準挑戰。代理在兩個互補的軸上進行評估：主觀的十項能力標準和一個確定性的衡量標準，判斷是否獲得了更深層的披露。一個跨家庭小組稀釋了同家庭偏愛；一個項目反應理論模型將代理質量與評審嚴格性分開。理論確定了測量內容和角色的結構；真實數據提供事件、歷史和概況——理論的覆蓋，數據的真實性。排名在兩種語言中都是可重複的（rho = 0.996 ZH / 0.953 EN）。對 28 個代理的評估揭示了被聚合分數掩蓋的能力水平差異。情緒調節和校準挑戰仍然是常見的弱點；保持模糊性是最具區分性的。角色扮演代理排名接近底部：沉浸並不意味著關係能力。對於所有代理，主要的失敗模式是用表面的溫暖替代實質的關係支持。我們將發布 500 對中英文平行對和評估代碼。
